long_biography.plain_text:
Williams International's expansion has been built around highly integrated factories that turn raw material into finished gas-turbine engines. As its owner-operator, Gregg G. Williams has overseen commercial and military product growth, including improved FJ33 and FJ44 engines and new production capacity. His involvement is technical as well as managerial: a mechanical-engineering graduate and named inventor, he previously led advanced technology, programme management and engineering inside the company.

Williams assumed full ownership and operating control of the family enterprise in 1999. The company had been founded by his father, engineer Sam Williams, whose compact-turbine work established its original technology base. Gregg later succeeded him as chairman while retaining operational leadership. He also holds separate manufacturing and medical-technology investments, but those roles are distinct from the Williams International business that anchors his wealth.

uncertainties: The exact person is resolved at very high confidence. The middle initial, company, American identity, age, technical career and current role align across government, SEC and first-party sources; the unrelated football coach has a different birth date and occupation.

The existing 4 February 1959 birth date is consistent with the age of 65 reported as of April 2024, but no strong public source located in this pass states the exact day and month. The existing date is retained without a proposal.
No reliable public source identified a birthplace or a second nationality, so those fields remain unproposed rather than inferred from company locations or citizenship.

The wealth-origin classification uses Marriage / family transfer for the taxonomy's broader inter vivos family-transfer category. The Utah government states that Gregg fully owned the company from 1999, while his father remained alive until 2009; calling the mechanism an inheritance would therefore be less precise.

Gregg Williams did not found Williams International. His father, Sam Williams, founded the predecessor company; Gregg's relationship is active successor-operator and sole owner after a career through its engineering and management functions.

Recent title wording has changed from chairman, president and chief executive to chairman and Chief Visioneering Officer. Owner and Chairman is proposed as the durable known-for title; no unsupported assumption is made about the exact date or structure of the executive transition.

Ramos Arizpe Manufacturing and Vivani Medical are documented separate interests. They are not treated as the origin or primary sector because Williams International remains the wholly owned core operating company.
